entries.proposition: Design: multicentre retrospective observational registry study in 18 hospitals, no control group.
entries.snippet: This multicenter, retrospective, observational study was conducted in 18 Spanish hospitals

entries.proposition: Patients outside the approved syndromes were treated under a compassionate-use programme at physician discretion, so the "other DEE" group is selected by prescribers.
entries.snippet: Although FFA is approved for DS and LGS, some patients with other DEEs were treated within a compassionate‐use program when deemed suitable by participating physicians.

entries.proposition: Primary effectiveness endpoints are seizure counts and responder categories; non-seizure outcomes were clinician-recorded 7-point global impressions by domain, a secondary endpoint.
entries.snippet: Change in non‐seizure outcomes previously defined from baseline were evaluated using the 7‐point CGI scale, ranging from very much improved to very much worse.

entries.proposition: Of 166 patients, 83 had a genetic etiology; among the other-DEE group the genes listed include one patient with a WWOX variant (the variant is not given).
entries.snippet: one each in SCN1B and SCN8A (c.2952C>A, p.Asn984Lys, gain‐of‐function variant), WWOX, PCDH19, TSC1, and BCL11B

entries.proposition: Supplementary Table S7 lists the WWOX row (n=1): no seizure freedom, not a 50 percent responder, no worsening, no adverse event at 3, 6 or 12 months. The paper draws no conclusion for any single gene.
entries.snippet: SCN1B (n=1) SCN8A (n=1) WWOX (n=1) Response | | | Seizure freedom | 1 (100) | 0 (0) | 0 (0) Responder rate (≥50%) | 1 (100) | 0 (0) | 0 (0) Worsening | 0 (0) | 0 (0) | 0 (0)

entries.proposition: The authors state that, owing to small samples, no definitive conclusion can be drawn on etiology or genetic diagnosis.
entries.snippet: Owing to small sample sizes, we cannot draw definitive conclusions on the impact of etiology on effectiveness and safety.

entries.proposition: Median reduction in total seizures at 12 months was 68.8 percent (Wilcoxon p below .001).
entries.snippet: At 12 months, there was a median percentage reduction in seizure frequency of 68.8% for total seizures (p < .001; Wilcoxon test)

entries.proposition: In each diagnosis the paper reports no significant difference in the 12-month responder proportion by age band (Table 3 prints p values of .14, .99, .29 and .56 across the columns, in cells of 7 to 54 patients); a non-significant test in cells this small is not evidence that the proportions are equal, and the table, not this sentence, carries the counts.
entries.snippet: Within each diagnosis category, there was no significant difference in the proportion of responders to FFA
entries.anchor: Results, Responders by age and DEE diagnosis

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Proposition narrowed after the blind audit (OVERSHOOT). Was: Within each diagnosis the 12-month responder proportion did not differ by age band (Table 3 prints 101 of 165, 32 of 42 and 21 of 40 as the all-ages cells); the table, not this sentence, carries the counts. The original said the proportion 'did not differ by age band'; the source says 'no significant difference', and the same paragraph reports a higher LGS responder rate in adults. The quoted snippet, anchor and artefact are unchanged unless stated.

entries.proposition: Retention was 96.4, 86.1 and 77.1 percent at 3, 6 and 12 months; the text does not state how patients who stopped before 12 months enter the responder denominators.
entries.snippet: FFA treatment retention rates were 96.4% (160/166), 86.1% (143/166), and 77.1% (128/166) at 3, 6, and 12 months, respectively

entries.proposition: Non-seizure outcome counts: improvement in cognition 51 of 86 (59.3 percent), behavior 36 of 88, sleep 18 of 74, caregiver 30 of 67. The ratings cover 86, 88, 74 and 67 of the 166 patients, i.e. about 52, 53, 45 and 40 percent: more than half for cognition and behavior, fewer than half only for sleep and caregiver.
entries.snippet: Between baseline and the 12‐month visit, 51 of 86 participants (59.3%), 36 of 88 (40.9%), 18 of 74 (24.3%), and 30 of 67 participants (44.8%) with CGI data showed improvements in cognition, behavior, sleep and caregiver domains, respectively

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Proposition narrowed after the blind audit (OVERSHOOT). Was: Non-seizure outcome counts: improvement in cognition 51 of 86 (59.3 percent), behavior 36 of 88, sleep 18 of 74, caregiver 30 of 67 - fewer than half of the 166 patients have a rating in any domain. The original said 'fewer than half of the 166 patients have a rating in any domain', which is false for cognition (86 of 166) and behavior (88 of 166). The quoted snippet, anchor and artefact are unchanged unless stated.

entries.proposition: The authors acknowledge the global-impression scale is not a formal test.
entries.snippet: Although assessed using CGI rather than formal testing, these changes are clinically meaningful and reflect domains of high relevance to patients and caregivers.

entries.proposition: The limitations paragraph names retrospective design, no control group, recall and documentation bias and non-standardised titration and co-medication changes.
entries.snippet: Based on its retrospective, observational design and no control group, there is potential for selection and reporting biases.

entries.proposition: Figure 2: the cognition improved bar for all DEEs (n=86) contains a large "minimally improved" segment (about 34 points of the 59 percent), and the "other DEE" group (n=20) shows about 45 percent improved cognition and 15 percent much worse behaviour.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 2 stacked bars by domain and group; All DEEs cognition n=86: very much improved about 8, much improved about 17, minimally improved about 34 (green total about 59), no change about 37, worse about 4; other DEE n=20 cognition: about 5 very much, 15 much, 25 minimally, 55 no change; other DEE behaviour n=20: about 15 much worse and about 10 minimally worse; sleep other DEE n=17 about 12 much worse.

entries.proposition: Figure 1A: at 12 months in all DEEs (N=166) the bars read 15 percent seizure free, 41 percent at least 75 percent reduction, 61 percent at least 50 percent reduction and 16 percent worsening; the 50-percent bar is cumulative.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1A total seizures, All DEEs N=166, 12 months: 100% bar 15, >=75% bar 41, >=50% bar 61, worsening 16; at 3 months 16, 29, 50, 12; at 6 months 17, 33, 48, 20; Dravet 12 months 33, 62, 76, 14; other DEE 12 months 15, 28, 53, 20.

entries.proposition: Figure S2B: retention at about 12 months is about 0.93 in Dravet, 0.74 in LGS and 0.68 in other DEEs; the text gives p 0.015 for the group difference.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig S2B Kaplan-Meier retention: DS (n=42) plateau about 0.93 after about 9.7 months; LGS (n=84) about 0.74 from about 7.8 months; Other DEEs (n=40) about 0.68 from about 9.6 months; censoring ticks from about 10 months.

entries.proposition: The paper reports no valvulopathy or pulmonary hypertension and no relevant laboratory disturbance in this cohort; the cardiac monitoring was echocardiography at baseline and every 6 months.
entries.snippet: No relevant laboratory disturbances were observed, and no cases of cardiac valvulopathy or pulmonary hypertension were reported.

entries.proposition: In LGS the paper reports a higher responder rate in adults than in the youngest children, which it relates possibly to disease evolution, with the caveat that few LGS patients were in the younger groups.
entries.snippet: For patients with LGS, a higher responder rate was observed in adults vs children 0–6 or
